facts.fact_text: On 7 April 2003 at 17h00 a demonstration was held in the centre of Yerevan on the occasion of Mother's Day.
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 took place on the Mashtots Avenue next to the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան).
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 appears to have been of a political nature, and criticism of the Government and of the conduct of the 2003 Armenian presidential election was voiced at it.
The applicant alleged, and the Government did not dispute, that the demonstration of 7 April 2003 was organised by women.
The applicant alleged, and the Government did not dispute, that the demonstration of 7 April 2003 was attended by about 30,000 people, the majority of whom were female.
Traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant did not as such participate in the demonstration of 7 April 2003, since most men, including himself, were observing it from a distance, standing on both sides of Mashtots Avenue.
The task of the men observing the demonstration of 7 April 2003 from a distance, including the applicant, was to encourage the women and to prevent possible provocations.

According to the applicant, on his way home on 7 April 2003, about 100-150 metres away from the site of the demonstration, he was approached by two persons in civilian clothes who showed police identity papers.
According to the applicant, the two persons in civilian clothes who approached him on 7 April 2003 took him to the Central District Police Station of Yerevan.
At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the arresting police officers drew up a record of the applicant's arrest (արձանագրությաւն բերման ենթարկելու մասին).

The record of the applicant's arrest stated that the applicant had been 'arrested at around 17h30 on the Mashtots Avenue for obstructing traffic and behaving in an anti-social way at a demonstration'.
The applicant was subjected to a search at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan during which no illegal items were found.

The police officers drew up a record of an administrative offence (վարչական իրավախախտման արձանագրություն) stating that the applicant had 'participated in a demonstration, during which he violated public order'.
The applicant's actions were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք) as minor hooliganism.
The record of an administrative offence was signed by the applicant.
The applicant put his signature in the section of the record of an administrative offence certifying that he was made aware of his rights under Article 267 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicant alleged that he had initially refused to sign the record of an administrative offence and requested a lawyer.

The applicant alleged that his initial refusal to sign the record of an administrative offence and his request for a lawyer was the reason why he was kept at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan for the following five and a half hours.

The applicant alleged that during the period he was kept at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the police officers were persistently trying to convince him to sign the record of an administrative offence and to refuse a lawyer.
The applicant alleged that the police officers told him it was unnecessary to have a lawyer and spend money for such a minor case.

The applicant alleged that the police officers told him the case had been already pre-decided by their superiors, so a lawyer would only harm rather than help, and that he may end up spending quite some time at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan because of that.

The applicant alleged that the police officers told him that if he signed the record of an administrative offence and refused a lawyer, he would be immediately taken to a court, where at worst a small fine would be imposed and he would be released.
The applicant alleged that he finally succumbed and agreed to sign the record of an administrative offence and to refuse a lawyer.
The applicant's actions were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք) as minor hooliganism.

Article 9 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 provides that a person shall be liable to an administrative penalty for offences envisaged by the Code, if these offences by their nature do not attract a criminal penalty in accordance with the law.

Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 (no longer in force as of 16 December 2005) defines minor hooliganism as obscene swearing at a person or an offensive annoyance of a person in a public place and other similar actions which disturb public order and peace of citizens, and prescribes a fine, correctional labour, or administrative detention not exceeding 15 days.
Traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003.

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժնի պետ) that on 7 April 2003 the officers were on duty at the Mashtots Avenue, where a demonstration was being held and a great number of people were gathered.

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan that while on duty on 7 April 2003 they noticed one person who was obstructing traffic, behaving in an anti-social way and inciting others to follow his example.

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan that the person observed obstructing traffic and behaving in an anti-social way on 7 April 2003 was brought to the Central District Police Station of Yerevan.
The applicant's actions were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք) as minor hooliganism.
The applicant's actions were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք) as minor hooliganism.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, after a brief hearing, sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences to three days of administrative detention.

The judge's entire finding in the applicant's case amounted to the following sentence: 'On 7 April 2003 at around 17h00 ... on the Mashtots Avenue [the applicant], together with a group of people, obstructed street traffic, violated public order by making a loud noise, and incited other participants of the demonstration to do the same...'

According to the record of the court hearing — drawn up in calligraphic handwriting — the hearing in the applicant's case was held in public with the participation of the judge, a clerk and the applicant.
According to the record of the court hearing, no questions were put to the applicant.

According to the record of the court hearing, having familiarised himself with the materials prepared by the police, the applicant accepted that he had signed the record of an administrative offence but objected to being subjected to administrative liability since the incriminated acts had been committed also by others.

The applicant alleged, and the Government did not explicitly dispute, that the record of the court hearing was a fake and was drafted at some point after the hearing in order to create an appearance of lawfulness.
The applicant alleged that in reply he tried to present the circumstances of the case, petitioned judge M. to summon some witnesses and requested a lawyer.

The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 describes the summary procedure prescribed by the Administrative Code of Armenia as an authentic remnant of the Communist style of justice inherited from the Soviet era, which denies the person charged the right to inform his/her family or to request the immediate assistance of a lawyer, and enables a judge, under an arrangement for immediate trial in camera, to have him/her held for a fortnight maximum.
Article 24 of the Constitution of Armenia of 1995 (prior to the amendments introduced in 2005) provides that everyone has the right to express his opinion.
Article 24 of the Constitution of Armenia of 1995 (prior to the amendments introduced in 2005) provides that it is prohibited to force anyone to give up or change his opinion.

Article 24 of the Constitution of Armenia of 1995 (prior to the amendments introduced in 2005) provides that everyone has the right to freedom of expression, including the freedom to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any information medium regardless of frontiers.

Article 26 of the Constitution of Armenia of 1995 (prior to the amendments introduced in 2005) provides that citizens have the right to hold peaceful assemblies, rallies, processions and demonstrations without carrying arms.

Article 39 of the Constitution of Armenia of 1995 (prior to the amendments introduced in 2005) provides that everyone has the right to have his violated rights restored, as well as, in the determination of a charge against him, the right to a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal with a respect for equality of arms.

Article 40 of the Constitution of Armenia of 1995 (prior to the amendments introduced in 2005) provides that everyone has the right to legal assistance, and that in cases prescribed by law legal assistance is provided free of charge.

Article 40 of the Constitution of Armenia of 1995 (prior to the amendments introduced in 2005) provides that everyone has the right to have a defence counsel from the moment of his arrest, detention or accusation.

Article 44 of the Constitution of Armenia of 1995 (prior to the amendments introduced in 2005) provides that no restrictions may be placed on the exercise of the rights and freedoms guaranteed under Articles 23-27 of the Constitution other than such as are prescribed by law and are necessary in the interests of national security or public safety, for the protection of public order, health or morals, or for the protection of the rights, freedoms, honour and reputation of others.

On 14 April 2003 the applicant applied to a local human rights NGO called 'February 22nd' («Փետրվարի 22» իրավապաշտպան կազմակերպություն), complaining in detail about the events of 7 April 2003 and seeking its assistance.

The applicant submitted to the NGO 'February 22nd', inter alia, that the police officers had prompted him to sign a document refusing a lawyer, persuading him that a lawyer was not necessary in his case.

On 28 April 2003 the NGO 'February 22nd' complained to the General Prosecutor (ՀՀ գլխավոր դատախազ) on behalf of the applicant, seeking to institute criminal proceedings against the police officers and judge M.

By a letter of 27 May 2003 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Prosecutor (Կենտրոն և Նորք-Մարաշ համայնքների դատախազ) informed the NGO 'February 22nd' that the decision of 7 April 2003 had been well-founded and there were no grounds for lodging a protest.
